questions.q: The radius of first orbit in hydrogen atom is $5.3\times10^{-11}$ m. The kinetic energy E$_K$, potential energy E$_P$ and total energy E$_T$ of electron in first orbit are
questions.explanation: For the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen, total energy E$_T$ = -13.6 eV, kinetic energy E$_K$ = -E$_T$ = 13.6 eV, and potential energy E$_P$ = 2E$_T$ = -27.2 eV.

questions.q: Bohr's second postulate implies quantisation of
questions.explanation: Bohr's second postulate states that the angular momentum of the electron is quantised in integral multiples of $h/2\pi$.

questions.q: An electron transition takes place from excited state to ground state in hydrogen atom, then
options: Its kinetic energy increases but potential energy and total energy decrease
Its kinetic energy, potential energy and total energy decrease
Kinetic energy decreases, potential energy increases but total energy remains same
Kinetic energy and total energy decrease but potential energy increases
questions.explanation: As the electron falls to a lower orbit, its kinetic energy ($=-E_n$) increases while both the potential energy and total energy become more negative, i.e., decrease.

questions.q: If the radius of first Bohr orbit is r, then the radius of the second Bohr orbit will be
questions.explanation: Bohr radius $r_n \propto n^2$, so for $n=2$, $r_2 = 4r_1 = 4r$.

questions.q: In alpha particle scattering experiment, if v is the initial velocity of the particle, then the distance of closest approach is d. If the velocity is doubled, then the distance of closest approach becomes
questions.explanation: The distance of closest approach $d\propto\dfrac{1}{v^2}$, so doubling v reduces d to $\dfrac{d}{4}$.

questions.q: The ratio of area of first excited state to ground state of orbit of hydrogen atom is
questions.explanation: Orbit radius $r\propto n^2$, so area $\propto r^2\propto n^4$; for $n=2$ versus $n=1$, the ratio is $2^4:1^4=16:1$.

questions.q: In the Rutherford's alpha scattering experiment, as the impact parameter increases, the scattering angle of the alpha particle
questions.explanation: A larger impact parameter means the alpha particle passes farther from the nucleus, experiencing weaker repulsion and hence smaller deflection (scattering angle decreases).

questions.q: Three energy levels of hydrogen atom and the corresponding wavelength of the emitted radiation due to different electron transition are as shown [E$_3$ at top, E$_2$ middle, E$_1$ bottom; $\lambda_3$ is the E$_3\to$E$_2$ transition, $\lambda_1$ is the E$_2\to$E$_1$ transition, $\lambda_2$ is the direct E$_3\to$E$_1$ transition]. Then
questions.explanation: Energy conservation: (E$_3$−E$_1$) = (E$_3$−E$_2$)+(E$_2$−E$_1$), i.e. hc/λ$_2$ = hc/λ$_3$+hc/λ$_1$, giving $\lambda_2=\lambda_1\lambda_3/(\lambda_1+\lambda_3)$.

questions.q: In accordance with the Bohr's model, the quantum number that characterises the Earth's revolution around the Sun in an orbit of radius 1.5 $\times$ 10$^{11}$ m with orbital speed 3 $\times$ 10$^4$ m s$^{-1}$ [given mass of Earth = 6 $\times$ 10$^{24}$ kg] is
questions.explanation: Angular momentum $L=mvr=6\times10^{24}\times3\times10^4\times1.5\times10^{11}=2.7\times10^{40}$ kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$. Using $L=n\hbar$, $n=L/\hbar \approx 2.7\times10^{40}/1.055\times10^{-34}\approx 2.57\times10^{74}$.

questions.q: An electron is revolving in its Bohr orbit having Bohr radius of 0.529 Å, then the radius of third orbit is
The radius of hydrogen atom in the ground state is 0.53 Å. After collision with an electron, it is found to have a radius of 2.12 Å, the principal quantum number 'n' of the final state of the atom is
Energy of an electron in the second orbit of hydrogen atom is E$_2$. The energy of electron in the third orbit of He$^+$ will be

The figure shows standing de Broglie waves due to the revolution of electron in a certain orbit of hydrogen atom (the loops shown correspond to the orbit's quantum number n = 4). Then the expression for the orbit radius is (all notations have their usual meanings)
questions.explanation: Bohr radius $r_n=\dfrac{n^2h^2\epsilon_0}{\pi me^2}$. The exact number of standing-wave loops in the figure is hard to read precisely, which is likely why the KEA awarded grace marks; taking n = 4 (as per the option matching the key) gives $r_4=\dfrac{16h^2\epsilon_0}{\pi me^2}$.

questions.q: An electron in an excited state of Li$^{2+}$ ion has angular momentum $\dfrac{3h}{2\pi}$. The de Broglie wavelength of electron in this state is P$\pi$a$_0$ (where a$_0$ = Bohr radius). The value of P is
questions.explanation: Angular momentum $\dfrac{3h}{2\pi}=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}\Rightarrow n=3$. Radius $r_n=\dfrac{n^2a_0}{Z}=\dfrac{9a_0}{3}=3a_0$. de Broglie wavelength $\lambda=\dfrac{2\pi r_n}{n}=\dfrac{2\pi(3a_0)}{3}=2\pi a_0=P\pi a_0 \Rightarrow P=2$.

questions.q: The de-Broglie wavelength associated with the electron of hydrogen atom in its ground state is
questions.explanation: In the ground state $2\pi r_1=\lambda$ (n=1), and $r_1=0.529$ Å, so $\lambda=2\pi(0.529)\approx3.3$ Å.

questions.q: Angular momentum of an electron in a hydrogen atom is $\dfrac{3h}{2\pi}$ (h is the Planck's constant). The K.E. of the electron is
questions.explanation: $L=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}=\dfrac{3h}{2\pi}\Rightarrow n=3$; K.E. $=\dfrac{13.6}{n^2}=\dfrac{13.6}{9}\approx1.51$ eV.

questions.q: A beam of fast moving alpha particles were directed towards a thin film of gold. The parts A, B and C of the transmitted and reflected beams corresponding to the incident parts A, B and C of the beam are shown in the adjoining diagram [A is the outermost, largest impact-parameter part of the beam; C passes closest to the nucleus]. The number of alpha particles in
options: C′ will be minimum and in B′ maximum
B′ will be minimum and in C′ maximum
A′ will be maximum and in C′ minimum
A′ will be minimum and in B′ maximum
questions.explanation: Since most of the atom is empty space, alpha particles with the largest impact parameter (part A) pass through almost undeflected in largest numbers, while very few (part C, aimed closest to the nucleus) get backscattered, so A′ is maximum and C′ is minimum (as per KEA key; question was graced, likely for wording/diagram ambiguity).

questions.q: The period of revolution of an electron revolving in the n$^{th}$ orbit of H-atom is proportional to
questions.explanation: Since $r\propto n^2$ and $v\propto 1/n$, $T=2\pi r/v\propto n^3$.

questions.q: In Rutherford experiment, for head-on collision of $\alpha$-particles with a gold nucleus, the impact parameter is
questions.explanation: For a head-on collision the alpha particle is aimed directly at the nucleus, so its impact parameter (perpendicular offset) is zero.

questions.q: Frequency of revolution of an electron revolving in n$^{th}$ orbit of H-atom is proportional to
questions.explanation: For the Bohr model, orbital radius $r_n \propto n^2$ and speed $v_n \propto 1/n$, so frequency $f = v_n/(2\pi r_n) \propto 1/n^3$.

questions.q: A hydrogen atom in ground state absorbs 10.2 eV of energy. The orbital angular momentum of the electron is increased by
questions.explanation: Absorbing 10.2 eV takes the electron from n = 1 to n = 2 (since $13.6(1-1/4)=10.2$ eV); the angular momentum increase is $(n_2-n_1)h/2\pi = h/2\pi = 1.05\times10^{-34}$ Js.

questions.q: The total energy of an electron revolving in the second orbit of hydrogen atom is
questions.explanation: Total energy E$_n$ = −13.6/n² eV; for n = 2, E$_2$ = −13.6/4 = −3.4 eV.

questions.q: The period of revolution of an electron in the ground state of hydrogen atom is T. The period of revolution of the electron in the first excited state is
questions.explanation: Time period T$_n$ ∝ n³; for the first excited state n = 2, T$_2$ = 2³T = 8T.

questions.q: The scientist who is credited with the discovery of 'nucleus' in an atom is
questions.explanation: Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment led to the discovery of the atomic nucleus.

questions.q: The energy (in eV) required to excite an electron from n = 2 to n = 4 state in hydrogen atom is
Total energy of electron in an excited state of hydrogen atom is -3.4 eV. The kinetic and potential energy of electron in this state
questions.explanation: For the Bohr model, $K=-E=3.4$ eV and $U=2E=-6.8$ eV.

questions.q: When electron jumps from n = 4 level to n = 1 level, the angular momentum of electron changes by
questions.explanation: $L_n=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$. $\Delta L=L_4-L_1=\dfrac{4h}{2\pi}-\dfrac{h}{2\pi}=\dfrac{3h}{2\pi}$.

questions.q: An α-particle of energy 5 MeV is scattered through 180° by gold nucleus. The distance of closest approach is of the order of
questions.explanation: $r_0=\dfrac{2kZe^2}{E}=\dfrac{2\times9\times10^9\times79\times(1.6\times10^{-19})^2}{8\times10^{-13}}\approx4.5\times10^{-14}$ m $\approx10^{-12}$ cm.

questions.q: If an electron in hydrogen atom jumps from an orbit of level n = 3 to an orbit of level n = 2, the emitted radiation has a frequency (R = Rydberg constant, C = velocity of light)
questions.explanation: $f=RC\left(\dfrac{1}{2^2}-\dfrac{1}{3^2}\right)=RC\left(\dfrac14-\dfrac19\right)=\dfrac{5RC}{36}$.

questions.q: What is the wavelength of light for the least energetic photon emitted in the Lyman series of the hydrogen spectrum. (take hc = 1240 eV nm)
questions.explanation: Least energetic Lyman transition is $n=2\to1$: $E=13.6(1-1/4)=10.2$ eV; $\lambda=hc/E=1240/10.2\approx122$ nm.

questions.q: Which of the following spectral series of hydrogen atom is lying in visible range of electromagnetic wave?
questions.explanation: The Balmer series (transitions to n=2) lies in the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: What is the energy of the electron revolving in third orbit expressed in eV?
Pick out the correct statement from the following :
options: Mercury vapour lamp produces line emission spectrum.
Oil flame produces line emission spectrum.
Band spectrum helps us to study molecular structure.
Sunlight spectrum is an example for line absorption spectrum.
questions.explanation: A mercury vapour lamp gives a discrete line emission spectrum; band spectra (from molecules) are used to study molecular structure; and the Fraunhofer lines in sunlight form a line absorption spectrum — so statements (1), (3) and (4) are all correct (an oil flame does not give a clean line spectrum).

questions.q: The ionisation energy of an electron in the ground state of helium atom is 24.6 eV. The energy required to remove both the electron is
questions.explanation: Removing the first electron needs the given 24.6 eV. The remaining electron sees a hydrogen-like ion with $Z=2$, needing $13.6\times2^2=54.4$ eV. Total $=24.6+54.4=79$ eV.

questions.q: [energy-level diagram of an atom showing three levels: 3E, 5E/3 and E] The figure shows the energy level of certain atom. When the electron deexcites from 3E to E, an electromagnetic wave of wavelength $\lambda$ is emitted. What is the wavelength of the electromagnetic wave emitted when the electron deexcites from $\dfrac{5E}{3}$ to E ?
questions.explanation: $\lambda\propto1/\Delta E$. $\Delta E(3E\to E)=2E$ gives $\lambda$; $\Delta E(5E/3\to E)=2E/3$, one-third as much, so its wavelength is three times as long: $3\lambda$.

questions.q: Spectrum of sunlight is an example for
questions.explanation: Sunlight from the hot photosphere passing through the cooler outer layers of the sun produces dark Fraunhofer lines superposed on it, so it is classified as a line absorption spectrum.

questions.q: In hydrogen atom, electron excites from ground state to a higher energy state and its orbital velocity is reduced to $\dfrac13$rd of its initial value. The radius of the orbit in the ground state is R. The radius of the orbit in that higher energy state is...........
questions.explanation: In the Bohr model $v \propto 1/n$ and $r \propto n^2$; since v becomes v/3, n becomes 3, so the new radius is $3^2R = 9R$.

questions.q: The ratio of the magnetic dipole moment to the angular momentum of the electron in the 1$^{st}$ orbit of hydrogen atom is
questions.explanation: For an orbiting electron, magnetic moment $\mu = \dfrac{e}{2m}L$, so the gyromagnetic ratio $\mu/L = e/2m$, independent of the orbit number.

questions.q: If n is the orbit number of the electron in a hydrogen atom, the correct statement among the following is
options: electron energy increases as n increases
hydrogen emits infrared rays for the electron transition from n=$\infty$ to n=1
electron energy is zero for n=1
questions.explanation: $E_n=-13.6/n^2$ eV becomes less negative (increases) as n increases; the n=$\infty\to1$ transition is the highest-energy Lyman line (UV, not infrared), E$_1$ is the most negative (not zero), and E$_n\propto1/n^2$, not n$^2$.

questions.q: Rutherford's atomic model could account for .................
options: the positively charged central core of an atom
questions.explanation: Rutherford's scattering experiment established the existence of a small, positively charged, massive nucleus (central core) at the center of the atom.

questions.q: When an electron jumps from the orbit $n=2$ to $n=4$, then wavelength of the radiations absorbed will be ................. ($R$ is Rydberg's constant).
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda}=R\left(\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{16}\right)=\dfrac{3R}{16} \Rightarrow \lambda=\dfrac{16}{3R}$.

questions.q: The ratio of minimum wavelengths of Lyman and Balmer series will be .................
questions.explanation: Minimum (series-limit) wavelengths: $\lambda_{Lyman}=1/R$, $\lambda_{Balmer}=4/R$; ratio $=1/4=0.25$.

questions.q: The spectrum of an oil flame is an example for .....................
questions.explanation: An oil flame contains glowing (incandescent) soot/carbon particles which emit a continuous emission spectrum, unlike gas-discharge sources which give line or band spectra.

questions.q: An electron is moving in an orbit of a hydrogen atom from which there can be a maximum of six transitions. An electron is moving in an orbit of another hydrogen atom from which there can be a maximum of three transitions. The ratio of the velocity of the electron in these two orbits is .....................
questions.explanation: Maximum transitions from level $n$ is $n(n-1)/2$; 6 transitions give $n=4$, and 3 transitions give $n=3$. Since $v\propto1/n$, the ratio $=v_4/v_3=(1/4)/(1/3)=3/4$.

questions.q: $\upsilon_1$ is the frequency of the series limit of Lyman series, $\upsilon_2$ is the frequency of the first line of Lyman series and $\upsilon_3$ is the frequency of the series limit of the Balmer series. Then ......
questions.explanation: $\upsilon_1=Rc$ (Lyman limit), $\upsilon_2=\tfrac34Rc$ (first Lyman line), $\upsilon_3=\tfrac14Rc$ (Balmer limit). Hence $\upsilon_1-\upsilon_2=\tfrac14Rc=\upsilon_3$.

questions.q: The de-Broglie wavelength of the electron in the ground state of the hydrogen atom is ............................ (radius of the first orbit of hydrogen atom = 0.53 \AA).
questions.explanation: For $n=1$, $mvr=h/2\pi\Rightarrow\lambda=h/mv=2\pi r=2\pi\times0.53=3.33$ \AA.

questions.q: The spectral series of the hydrogen atom that lies in the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum
questions.explanation: The Balmer series (transitions to $n=2$) lies in the visible region of the hydrogen spectrum.

questions.q: Continuous emission spectrum is produced by
questions.explanation: A hot solid filament (incandescent lamp) emits a continuous blackbody-like spectrum, unlike vapour lamps which give line spectra.

questions.q: Hydrogen atom from excited state comes to the ground state by emitting a photon of wavelength λ. If R is the Rydberg constant, the principal quantum number 'n' of the excited state is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda}=R\left(1-\dfrac{1}{n^2}\right) \Rightarrow n^2=\dfrac{\lambda R}{\lambda R-1} \Rightarrow n=\sqrt{\dfrac{\lambda R}{\lambda R-1}}$.
